courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Civil/Architectural Blueprint Reading
courses.description: Reading and interpreting blueprints for civil engineering, architecture, and construction fields. No prior blueprint reading experience is needed. Course provides preparation for more advanced civil and architectural drafting coursework.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Introduction to Engineering
courses.description: The course explores the branches of engineering, the functions of an engineer, and the industries in which engineers work. Explains the engineering education pathways and explores effective strategies for students to reach their full academic potential. Presents an introduction to the methods and tools of engineering problem solving and design including the interface of the engineer with society and engineering ethics. Develops communication skills pertinent to the engineering profession. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Introduction to Civil Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to the Civil Engineering and the related fields of architecture and construction. Includes an overview of academic programs, career information and preparation requirements, possible field trips and guest speakers. CSU

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Solidworks Beginning Solid Modeling
courses.description: Introductory course in parametric solid modeling using Solidworks, an industry standard engineering design software (CAD). This course will include a solid modeling overview, solid model construction techniques (extrude, revolve, fillet, chamfer, etc.), including the preparation of individual solid components and basic solid model assemblies. (Same as Manufacturing Technology 103). CSU

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Solidworks Intermediate Solid Modeling
courses.description: Intermediate course for solid modeling using Solidworks, an industry standard engineering design software (CAD). Includes a review of the introductory class and changes to the Solidworks interface. Instruction in the use of intermediate Solidworks part modeling skills such as assembly modeling and sub-assemblies is included (Same as Manufacturing Technology 104). (Same as Manufacturing Technology 104). CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Solidworks Advanced Solid Modeling
courses.description: Advanced course for solid modeling includes a review of the intermediate class and changes to the Solidworks interface. Instruction in the use of Solidworks part modeling, assembly modeling, sub-assemblies, advanced photoworks and advanced animator emphasized (Same as Manufacturing Technology 105). (Same as Manufacturing Technology 105). CSU

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Basic Mechanical Blueprint Reading
courses.description: Reading and interpreting blueprints for manufacturing technologies. (Same as Manufacturing Technology 111). CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing
courses.description: Drawing interpretation utilizing geometric dimensioning and tolerancing per ASME Y14.5M (formerly ANSI Y14.5M) as applied in engineering, manufacturing, and inspection. Suggested preparation: prior course or experience in drafting with conventional dimensioning and tolerancing. (Same as Manufacturing Technology 114). CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Surveying
courses.description: The course applies theory and principles of plane surveying: office computations and design; operation of surveying field equipment; and production of engineering plans/maps. Topics include distances, angles, and directions; differential leveling; traversing; property/boundary surveys; topographic surveys/mapping; volume/earthwork; horizontal and vertical curves; land description techniques; and GPS. Field work using tapes, levels, transits, theodolites, total stations, and GPS. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Advanced Plane Surveying
courses.description: A second course in surveying with emphasis on coordinate geometry calculations. Topics include: route surveying with horizontal and vertical curves, topographic surveying and mapping, construction surveying, introduction to geospatial technologies, boundary surveying and surveys of public lands. Field surveying projects. Completion of Engr 118 and 119 assists in passing the land-surveyor-in-training (LSIT) exam. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Engineering Drawing
courses.description: Principles of engineering drawing: projections, views, sections, dimensions, tolerancing, assemblies, manufacturing processes, engineering drafting practices. Utilizing 2D CAD and 3D solid modeling CAD software. Suggested preparation: prior course or experience in drafting and CAD. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Engineering Graphics
courses.description: This course covers the principles of engineering drawings in visually communicating engineering designs and an introduction to computer-aided design (CAD). Topics include: the development of visualization skills; orthographic projections; mechanical dimensioning and tolerancing practices; the engineering design process. Assignments develop sketching skills for 2-D and 3-D CAD. The use of CAD software is an integral part of the course. Suggested preparation: prior course or experience with drafting and CAD. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Introduction to Robotics
courses.description: Introductory course in robotics. Topics include: basic design, sensors, actuators, circuits, programming, micro-controllers, and a hands-on robot construction project. CSU

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Mechatronics I
courses.description: A first course in mechatronics. Topics emphasize hands-on work and include: solid modeling design, microcontrollers and programming, rapid prototype fabrication, testing, measurement, actuators, sensors, and basic electronics. Prior experience with Solidworks, Arduino, and basic algebra is suggested but not required. CSU

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Mechatronics II
courses.description: A second course in mechatronics. Topics emphasize hands-on work and include: solid-modeling design, rapid prototype fabrication, testing, measurement, micro-controllers, programming, industrial robotics, and PLC control. Prior experience or coursework in Solidworks, Arduino, and basic algebra is strongly suggested. CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Revit and Civil Drafting
courses.description: Course introduces Autodesk Revit, a 3D parametric CAD software that is an industry standard for architectural/civil design. Topics include 3D modeling, design, drawing creation, and BIM (building information modeling) concepts. Course also teaches creation of industry-standard drawings in civil engineering, architecture, and construction using industry-standard CAD software (AutoCAD, Civil 3D, and Revit). Topics include - views, line types, projection, annotations, and callouts. Prior course or experience with AutoCAD (e.g., Engr 183) and drafting is strongly suggested. CSU

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Basic Machining Concepts and Operations
courses.description: Fundamental operations on lathes, milling machines, grinders, and drill presses, including precision measurements and layout. Equips students with skills and theory necessary to enter or upgrade within the machinist trade. (Same as Manufacturing Technology 158). (Same as Manufacturing Technology 158). CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: AutoCAD I
courses.description: A first course in AutoCAD by Autodesk, an industry standard engineering CAD software, especially in the civil and architectural fields. Topics include display and file management, units, entities, object selection, advanced editing, layers, dimensions, text, and graphic exchange. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: AutoCAD II
courses.description: A second course in Autodesk AutoCAD, an industry standard engineering CAD software, especially in the civil and architectural fields. Topics include: advanced dimensioning, viewports, hatches, blocks, plotting, attributes, inquiry, intermediate apps, working drawings, introduction to 3D CAD. Suggested preparation: prior course or experience with AutoCAD. CSU

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Civil 3D
courses.description: Course teaches Autodesk Civil 3D - an industry standard CAD software for civil engineers. Topics include advanced modeling, model merging, project management, parcels, surveys, surfaces, alignments, profiles, 3D rendering, and presentation. Prior coursework or experience with AutoCAD is strongly suggested. CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Statics
courses.description: A first course in engineering mechanics: properties of forces, moments, couples and resultants; two- and three-dimensional force systems acting on engineering structures in equilibrium; analysis of trusses, and beams; distributed forces, shear and bending moment diagrams, center of gravity, centroids, friction, and area and mass moments of inertia. Utilizes SI metrics. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Dynamics
courses.description: Fundamentals of kinematics and kinetics of particles and rigid bodies. Topics include kinematics of particle motion; Newton's second law, work-energy and momentum methods; kinematics of planar motions of rigid bodies; work-energy and momentum principles for rigid body motion; Introduction to mechanical vibrations. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Electric Circuits
courses.description: An introduction to the analysis of electrical circuits. Use of analytical techniques based on the application of circuit laws and network theorems. Analysis of DC and AC circuits containing resistors, capacitors, inductors, dependent sources, operational amplifiers, and/or switches. Natural and forced responses of first and second order RLC circuits; the use of phasors; AC power calculations; power transfer; and energy concepts. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Electric Circuits Laboratory
courses.description: An introduction to the construction and measurement of electrical circuits. Basic use of electrical test and measurement instruments including multimeters, oscilloscopes, power supplies, and function generators. Interpretation of measured data under DC, transient, and sinusoidal steady-state (AC) conditions. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Strength of Materials
courses.description: This course is a study of stresses, strains and deformations associated with axial, torsional and flexural loading of bars, shafts and beams, as well as pressure loading of thin-walled pressure vessels. The course also covers stress and strain transformation, Mohr's Circle, ductile and brittle failure theories, and the buckling of columns. Statically indeterminate systems are also studied. CSU/UC

notes: CU0002 is parsed explicitly; unrecognized catalog layouts are not guessed.
Crosswalk ownership is college-aware; ambiguous ownership remains flagged instead of silently assigned.
CU0321 last-offered data is a planning signal only and does not determine curriculum currency.
DO NOT SCHEDULE rooms are owner-only when a matching owner division is present; they are not campuswide rooms.
Shared portal writes are revalidated server-side; browser-calculated totals are not trusted.
Local database mode writes proposals to SQLite with revision history and stores per-department draft workspaces; static HTML is preview-only for database actions.
Department draft workspaces are isolated by term/college/division/department so switching scope does not destroy unfinished work.
2026-27 credit default is Standardized Attendance Accounting; open-entry/open-exit credit remains Actual Hours / Positive Attendance.
Faculty load caps/factors are configurable planning values, not a contractual certification.
Pathway membership comes only from a confirmed administrator-provided mapping; it is never inferred from course title, TOP code, or division.
Imported existing bookings are a snapshot at generation time, not a live Ad Astra/Colleague connection; regenerate after refreshing the booking export.
Empty optional booking/pathway CSV files are ignored with import warnings; malformed or headerless files produce a clear validation error instead of a raw csv traceback.
RG0547 prepopulation maps prior dates by relative term week + weekday; previous CRNs are retained only as a reference and are never reused as current-term identifiers.
Block schedule alignment is advisory. The planner suggests approved windows and permits documented exceptions rather than blocking CTE/long-format schedules.
Department-chair modality labels are translated to scheduler/Colleague codes from the imported DE coding reference when available.
